root_cause.text: The `intel_pmu_hw_config` function fails to verify if sibling events in an auto counter reload group are x86 events before passing them to `intel_pmu_set_acr_caused_constr`, which performs an unsafe `container_of` cast on non-x86 (software) event PMUs.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the addition of an `is_x86_event(sibling)` check inside the `for_each_sibling_event` loop in `arch/x86/events/intel/core.c` before calling `intel_pmu_set_acr_caused_constr(sibling, ...)`. The commit message explains that software events do not use `x86_hybrid_pmu`, and performing a `container_of` operation on them via the hybrid helper in `intel_pmu_set_acr_caused_constr` causes out-of-bounds memory reads.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard check to ensure sibling events are x86 events before applying Intel PMU constraints.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check `if (is_x86_event(sibling))` inside the loop that iterates over sibling events in `intel_pmu_hw_config`.
intent_record.how: Ensures that Intel PMU address-range filtering constraints are only applied to x86 PMU events, preventing unsafe operations on non-x86 sibling events.
